Sure thing! I’ll help you bump the core dependencies and tooling in your Cursor‑built Next.js project to the newest stable release. Since you’re not a developer, we’ll keep the steps clean and give you the exact clicks or commands to run. I’m assuming your app already has a basic login or user data stored, so we’ll treat it as **Amber** risk (since you’re updating a web app that may touch user data). We’ll keep a save point before every change, so you can roll back if anything goes wrong. --- ## 1️⃣ Overview – What we’re doing ``` What we are building: Upgrade Next.js (and related core libs) to the latest version. Who uses it: Your users, no new public facing changes. Risk level: Amber – because the code may touch logged‑in users or private data. Day‑one features: Just a newer framework, nothing new for users. Information it stores: Same as before (users, posts, etc.), no new private fields. Logins: Same provider – we’ll keep the auth logic unchanged. Money: No payments added. Built with: Next.js 15.0.4 (latest) – new app features & performance improvements. Steps: 1. Make a checkpoint (Git commit or zip). 2. Install new Next.js, React, and supporting libs. 3. Update scripts & config files. 4. Re‑run tests (if you have them) or check the dev server. 5. Push changes, redeploy on Cursor. Safety notes: • All secret keys stay in `.env`/Cursor Secrets. • We’ll enable guardian PWA/SSR/SSG defaults that ship with the new Next.js. • We’ll create automated test‑run snippets so you can verify quickly. ``` **Does this look right?** Reply `yes` or let me know if you’d like a different approach. --- ## 2️⃣ Step‑by‑step guide > *Please copy the exact lines in bold when you run them. > For the commands, open a terminal in your project folder (Cursor → “Terminal” → “New Terminal”). > After each main change, I’ll note the save point.* --- ### 2.1 Create a safe checkpoint 1. **If you have Git**
```bash git add . git commit -m "🔒 checkpoint before Next.js upgrade" ``` *(We commit all current files to stay safe.)* 2. **If you don’t have Git**
Download the folder as a zip, add your current timestamp to the file name like `myapp_2026-11-22_backup.zip`. *(Keep the zip in a safe place.)* > **Save point created: “checkpoint_before_upgrade_2026-11-22”.** --- ### 2.2 Install the latest Next.js and React > **What will happen:** > `next@15`, `react@18`, `react-dom@18` are pulled in. > These are the current LTS releases. > The `package.json` file will update automatically. 1. In the terminal, run: ```bash npm install next react react-dom ``` or if you use Yarn: ```bash yarn add next react react-dom ``` 2. **Confirm the new versions**: ```bash npm list next react react-dom ``` *You should see versions 15.x, 18.x.* --- ### 2.3 Update TypeScript / Babel if needed > *Cursor uses TS by default, but if you’re on an older TS, bump it.* ```bash npm install typescript@latest @types/react@latest @types/node@latest ``` --- ### 2.4 Update the `next.config.js` (if you have one) The new Next.js introduces a small config change: ```js /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ const nextConfig = { reactStrictMode: true, // New: Ensure Image optimization works with all domains images: { remotePatterns: [] } }; module.exports = nextConfig; ``` *Just keep your existing keys; add the `remotePatterns` line if you’re loading images from external sites.* --- ### 2.5 Check router imports From Next.js 15, the `next/link` and `next/router` imports stay the same, but some internal utilities changed. If you use `import { useRouter } from 'next/router'`, keep it unchanged; nothing else to do. --- ### 2.6 Run the development server ```bash npm run dev ``` or ```bash yarn dev ``` > **What to look for:** > • No build errors in the terminal. > • The site opens at `http://localhost:3000`. > • All pages load. > • If you have auth, log in as usual – nothing should break. If everything looks fine, create another small commit or zip for the new state: ```bash git add . git commit -m "✅ Next.js 15 migration complete" ``` > **Checkpoint: “after_great_migration_2026-11-22”.** --- ### 2.7 (Optional) Update other common packages If you’re using `styled-components`, `axios`, `next-auth`, or any GraphQL client, bump them to compatible latest versions. Example for `next-auth`: ```bash npm install next-auth@latest ``` > *If you get compatibility warnings, follow the package’s docs to resolve them.* --- ### 2.8 Push changes to Cursor 1. Commit and push: ```bash git push origin main ``` *Cursor will trigger a rebuild automatically.* 2. In Cursor, go to **“Deployments”** → **“Rebuild”** → **Confirm**. *Wait for the build to finish (it should report “Success”).* 3. Open the live URL to confirm everything works. --- ## 3️⃣ Quick sanity check *Run a simple test by visiting:* - `https://your-cursor-app.vercel.app/` – see your homepage. - Log in if you use auth. - Create, edit, or view a page that touches user data. - Check the browser console for errors.
